## (c) TRAPS — symptom, root cause, fix

### Trap 1 — Type metrics silently invalidate a threshold decision

**Symptom.** A column cap chosen and verified as correct started wrapping a label in the
wrong place after the real font was self-hosted. `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY` began wrapping
after "OF" instead of after "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT".

**Root cause.** The 160px cap was calibrated against fallback-font metrics. Under Futura
Round every label got ~12% narrower, and `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` dropped to 132.9px — now
inside 160.

**Diagnostic.** Post-font measurements versus Figma:

| Label | Fallback | Futura Round | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| ORDERS & SHIPPING | 120 | **106** | 106 ✅ exact |
| OUR STORY | 68 | **60** | 60 ✅ exact |
| BOOK AN APPOINTMENT | 149 | **131** | 135 |

**Fix.** Re-derive every content-driven threshold after the real font loads. Two prior
findings resolved themselves automatically (the mobile BOOK wrap and an 18px overflow at
768px). `[CONFIRMED]`

**Related trap — `document.fonts.check()` is useless for availability.** It returned `true`
for every family queried, including ones definitively not installed. Only **width comparison
against a known-generic family** is reliable:

```js
const measure = fam => { const s = document.createElement('span');
  s.style.cssText = `position:absolute;white-space:nowrap;font-size:12px;font-weight:500;
    letter-spacing:0;text-transform:uppercase;font-family:${fam}`;
  s.textContent = 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT'; document.body.appendChild(s);
  const w = s.getBoundingClientRect().width; s.remove(); return Math.round(w*10)/10; };
```

Results: full declared stack **149.1**; `'Futura'` **149.1** (identical → this is what
renders); `'Futura Round'` / `'Futura LT Pro'` / `'Century Gothic'` / `sans-serif` /
`monospace` all **140.7** (→ none installed, all falling through to the same default);
`'Gill Sans'` 137.8; `'Arial'` 143.4.

`[RETRACTED]` The session repeatedly claimed the fallback rendered "Century Gothic / Gill
Sans"; the probe proved it was macOS system **Futura**. And the "~13% wider" figure is
macOS-specific — vs generic sans it is ~6%.

### Trap 2 — A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line

**Symptom.** The ABOUT column sat at its 160px cap with 45px of dead space, pushing the
CONTACT column right and making the site map visibly disproportionate against Figma.

**Diagnostic.**

| Column | Box | Longest line | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABOUT** | **160** | **115** | **45** |
| CONTACT | 135 | 131 | 4 |
| HELP | 105.6 | 105.6 | 0 |

**Root cause.** A wrapped element fills the width available to it. Only the *unwrapped*
siblings hug their content.

**Fix.** `width: min-content` on the wrapped item — resolves to the widest unbreakable run.
Result: About 160→115, slack 45→0, gaps redistributed 99.7→122.2px.

**Must be gated.** Applying it blindly is wrong: `Book an Appointment` went 131→76 and
wrapped. The session gated it on the presence of the NBSP (Trap 3), tying the sizing to the
same signal that already marks the break as intentional:

```tsx
sx={link.fields.label.includes(NBSP) ? { width: 'min-content' } : undefined}
```

`[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:497`.

### Trap 3 — No single threshold can satisfy two constraints; constrain the text instead

**Symptom.** No column cap value could both wrap label A after its first word and keep
label B on one line.

**Diagnostic.**

| Requirement | Constraint |
|---|---|
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` fits line 1 | cap ≥ 115px |
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` must NOT fit | cap < 132.9px |
| `Book an Appointment` stays one line | cap ≥ 131px |

**Viable window: [131, 132.9) — 1.9 pixels.** That is a coincidence, not a tolerance. Any
hinting difference or one-character copy edit breaks it.

**Fix.** Put the constraint on the phrase, not the container — a non-breaking space:

```ts
label: 'Acknowledgement of Country'
```

With one break opportunity left, the full string cannot fit any cap, so it *must* break
there. Safe window widens from 1.9px to 71px (any cap 115–186px). Use the ` ` escape,
not a literal character — an invisible byte in source is a trap for the next reader.

**Carries a content dependency.** In production this label comes from Contentful, so an
editor must author the NBSP there too; a plain space reverts the wrap. Document it and tell
the content team. `[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `contentfulFixture.ts:56` with that note.

### Trap 4 — `minHeight` + centred alignment loses all leading when content wraps

**Symptom.** The two-line nav label sat flush against the item above it; single-line
siblings looked correctly spaced.

**Diagnostic.**

| Item | box | leading above text |
|---|---|---|
| Our Story / Sustainability / Careers / Brand Protection | 24 | **4.5** |
| **Acknowledgement of Country** | 29 | **0** |

**Root cause.** `minHeight: 24px` + `alignItems: center`. Centring only distributes the
space a *single* line leaves over. Two lines are 29px, which overflows the 24px floor, so
there is nothing to distribute and the leading collapses to zero.

**Fix.** Derive height from `lineHeight` + `paddingBlock` so it holds at any line count.
Keep `minHeight` as the accessibility floor (24px target, WCAG 2.5.8) but stop using it to
*define* the height. Result: exactly 24 / 38, column total 134 = Figma's `Links` frame.

**Nuance worth preserving:** `minHeight` is still the right tool for **reserving** a slot
(so a content swap cannot clip), because it lets the box grow. The trap is only using
`minHeight` + centring to *derive* a height. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Trap 5 — A shorthand resets a longhand declared above it, in your own object

**Symptom.** The first version of the nav-item fix had literally no effect.

**Root cause.** `padding: 0` sat twelve lines *after* `paddingBlock: '4.5px'` in the same
recipe object, and reset it.

**Fix.** `paddingInline: 0` instead of the `padding` shorthand, with a comment so nobody
reintroduces it. `[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `zimmNavItem.ts:38`.

**Note:** the project's `recipeGuards.test.ts` does *not* catch this — it checks for bare
scale keys inside compound shorthands, not a shorthand resetting a longhand above it. A
known gap.

### Trap 6 — Inline-block / inline-flex descender leak inside a block `<li>`

**Symptom.** Item spacing 26px where Figma had 24, compounding to −6px by the third item.

**Diagnostic.**
```
liDisplay: "list-item"   liHeight: 26
aDisplay:  "inline-flex" aHeight:  24
```

**Root cause.** An `inline-flex` anchor inside a block `<li>` sits on a text baseline, so
the line-box strut adds descender space — measured at ~1.5–2px per row, 9px across five
rows.

**Fix.** `display: flex` on the `<li>`. `[CONFIRMED]` — this was the "C" mutation in Step 8
and closed Δ9 → Δ5 on the links column.

### Trap 7 — Gap ownership: whose 16px is it?

**Symptom.** The contact icon row sat 16px lower than Figma, and only the icon row.

**Root cause.** Figma nests `Icon-list` **inside** the `Links` stack as its 4th child with 0
gap. Our markup made `contactRow` a **sibling of the `<ul>`** inside a `display: flex;
gap: 16px` column — so it collected a gap Figma does not have.

**Fix.** Move the gap from the column to the heading — `linkCol { gap: 0 }` +
`columnHeading { marginBottom: 'm' }` — and move the icon row inside the `<ul>` as its last
`<li>`. `[CONFIRMED]` Whenever a spacing delta affects **one child and not its siblings**,
suspect gap ownership / DOM nesting rather than a wrong value.

### Trap 8 — An undesigned responsive band, and `nowrap` does not prevent shrinking

**Symptom.** Across 768–1022px all five legal links wrapped to two lines each, plus an 18px
horizontal scrollbar at exactly 768px.

**Root cause, in three steps.**
1. At `BP.tablet` (768px) the bottom bar switched from stacked to a single row.
2. That row needs ~845px of content: copyright 185 + five links 468 + six 32px gaps 192. At
   768px only ~554px is available after padding and the locale control.
3. **`flexWrap: nowrap` says "don't break onto a second line" — it does not say "don't
   shrink".** Flex items shrink by default. "TERMS & CONDITIONS" wants 118px and got 70px.
   The row refuses to break, so the words break instead.

**Diagnostic** (simulating the prior `whiteSpace: nowrap`):

| | link widths | link height | page overflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old (`nowrap`) | 74/118/84/96/96 — natural | 31px | **201px** |
| Now (`normal`) | 74/70/43/48/50 — squeezed | 45px | **18px** |

Neither is correct; the underlying defect is identical. Reporting this honestly mattered —
the earlier change had *reduced* the symptom by 90% while leaving the cause.

**Fix considered and DISCARDED.** Moving the row switch to `BP.desktop` (1024) fixed the
band (`ovf 18→0`, `navWrap 7→1`, `legalH 45→31`, 1022px+ byte-identical). It was discarded
because Figma specifies only 402 / 1023 / 1440 and all three already matched — so the change
was not spec compliance but a judgement call about an inferred state, costing +179–236px of
footer height.

**What shipped instead** — declare it and escalate, because the band is iPad portrait:

| Device | Portrait width | |
|---|---|---|
| iPad mini | 744 | below the band |
| iPad 10.2" / Air 11" / Pro 11" | 810 / 820 / 834 | **in it** |
| iPad Pro 13" | 1024 | above it |

Against a ≤10-defect / no-Sev3 contract, "Figma doesn't specify it" is not an accepted
defence once QA logs it. `[CONFIRMED]` One narrower change *was* shipped:
`bottomInner`'s gutter step moved from `BP.desktop` to `BP.tablet`, so the bottom bar stopped
sitting 8px left of the content above it across 768–1023px.

### Trap 9 — Inline vs inline-flex vertical padding, and a 1px chrome border

**Symptom.** "The copyright looks different from the legal links" — while every typographic
property matched byte-for-byte (10px / 500 / 14px line-height / 0.025rem tracking /
uppercase / same colour).

**Root cause.** Box model, not type:

| | Copyright | Legal link |
|---|---|---|
| Element | `<span>` — **inline** | `<a>` — **`inline-flex`** |
| `paddingY: xs` (8px) | applies visually but **does not affect layout height** | contributes to the box |
| Underline-mechanism border | — | **+1px** transparent bottom border on the inner span |
| Total | 30px | **31px** |

`alignItems: center` on the row then centres two *boxes* of different heights, and sub-pixel
rounding surfaces the 0.5px offset as a visible half-line shift. Figma agrees they should
match — it wraps Copyright in a Container frame of height 23, same as the `footer-item`
instances.

**Fix.** Give `copyright` the same box: `display: inline-flex` + `alignItems: center`. A
second finding fell out — `legalLink` carried `height: 'auto'`, silently overriding the
atom's designed 24px, an uncommented deliberate-looking override. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Trap 10 — A perceived SPACING defect can be a TYPE defect

**Symptom.** The user reported the subscribe block's spacing looked wrong.

**Investigation.** Both gaps were verified correct against Figma's own emitted values
(`alias/space/600` = 24px heading→body, `alias/space/1000` = 40px body→field) and matched the
code exactly.

**Root cause found instead.** The body copy was rendering at the wrong text style, so at the
same 200px max-width it wrapped differently — which changed the block height and the rhythm
all the way down to the email field, even though every gap was right.

`[UNVERIFIED / possibly retracted]` The session concluded Figma node `1892:50533` binds
`Default/body2` (14px / 400 / 18px) and changed `caption` → `body2`. **The shipped code today
has `textStyle: 'caption'`** with a comment asserting caption (12px / 500 / 18px). The
footer history was squashed into one commit so I cannot tell whether this was a deliberate
retraction or lost in the squash. **Worth re-checking against Figma** — it materially affects
wrapping, which was the original complaint.

The transferable lesson stands regardless: **before adjusting a gap, verify the type style**,
because wrapping is a function of type metrics and a wrap change reads as a spacing change.

### Trap 11 — Reserving a slot versus reproducing the design's anchoring

This one reversed twice and is the clearest example of getting a fidelity call wrong by
comparing against the wrong node.

**Symptom.** Submitting the subscribe form grew the footer by 22px (slot 45→68, column
163→186, footer 490→512).

**First diagnosis.** The child swaps `<form>` (45px = 36px content + 4/4 padding + 1px
border) for `<p>` (68px = 36px text + 16/16 padding). `subscribeSuccess` carried 32px of its
own vertical padding the form does not have; nothing reserved the slot.

**First fix.** A `subscribeControl` part with `minHeight: 45px`, and strip the message's
padding. Verified Δ0 at 1440 / 768 / 375 / 320.

**The mutation test that mattered.** Removing the padding *alone* showed Δ0 at desktop and
tablet — and that was **coincidence**: the message became 36px, *shorter* than the 45px form,
so the column shrank 9px and the taller site-map column absorbed it. Mobile, where columns
stack, exposed it (Δ−9). `minHeight` was load-bearing, just not where you would look.
**`[CONFIRMED]` Always mutation-test a layout fix at mobile, not desktop.**

**RETRACTION 1.** The session had asserted *"the design's slot is 59px in both states."* It
is not. `footer/textfield` has two variants — `Subscribed=False` 320×44 and `Subscribed=True`
308×59 (narrower too) — and the composed frames show the column staying flat by
**repositioning**: field 44→59 (+15) while the gap above shrinks 40→24 (−16). It is a
compensating reposition, not a reserved slot. Consequence: the subscribed message is a
documented component variant, so implementing it is a build task, not a designer question.

**RETRACTION 2 (the deeper one).** Read like-for-like from the composed page file:

```
                    Textfield        Subscribe Section
initial  4019:45515  y=82  320×44    126
error    4019:45927  y=82  320×61    143   (+17, error appended BELOW the input)
success  4019:46044  y=82  320×59    141   (+15, input replaced by a padded message)
site map                             158   ← 15px spare over the tallest
```

The field's **top stays at y=82 in every state and grows downward**. Neither state jumps —
purely because the column stays shorter than the site map. The success `Textfield` is
`16 + 27 (cap, 2 lines) + 16 = 59`, which in browser terms is `16 + 36 + 16 = 68` — **exactly
what we already had before the "fix"**. The reservation suppressed a growth the design
intends and made the message 23px shorter than specified.

**Why the residual is irreducible:**
```
design  top block  8 + 24 + 26 = 58   → 15px spare over the site map
ours    top block 18 + 24 + 36 = 78   → −6px
                  ───────────────
                  +20px cap-height inflation
```
The design budgeted 15px of headroom that browser text metrics do not leave. That is a real
question for the designer, not a code defect.

**Also found on the way, and a genuine conformance win:** the body's `marginBottom` was 40px
where the composed design specifies **24px** in every state. That 16px inflated the column
and consumed the headroom. Fixing it took @1440 Δ21→Δ5 and @768 Δ7→Δ0.

**Shipped state `[CONFIRMED from the repo]`:** the 45px reserved slot
(`SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'`, commit `9ec0740`), documented as PROVISIONAL with the
59px Figma reference in the comment. The 40→24 gap correction and the design-correct
restructure were **left uncommitted as an open decision** — `subscribeBody` still carries
`marginBottom: '3xl'` (40px) today. The trade was stated as: stillness (Δ0 everywhere, a
deviation) versus structure (matches Figma, Δ5–6 desktop and Δ22–23 mobile). Deferred to the
lead, correctly, after two wrong attempts.

**And a mobile-inherent limit:** the design's anti-jump property *is* headroom beside the
site map. Stacked, there is no neighbour — the design's own section grows 126→143 and would
move everything below it. A jump on mobile is inherent to an in-flow error message; only
reserving or taking it out of flow gives Δ0, and both are deviations.

### Trap 12 — A border cannot be inset

**Symptom.** The mobile divider above the logo ran full-bleed; Figma insets it 20px each
side (`x=20, width=362` in a 402 frame, bound to `alias/space/500`).

**Root cause.** Implemented as `borderTop` on the logo div. A border always spans its
element's full width. Figma models the divider as its own `Container` frame holding a vector.

**Fix.** A pseudo-element with matching `left`/`right` insets:
```ts
position: 'relative',
_before: { content: '""', position: 'absolute', top: 0,
           left: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
           height: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)', background: COLOUR_HALF_INV },
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { _before: { display: 'none' } },
```
Verified: 402px line 20→382; 767px line 20→747 (inset holds at any mobile width); no divider
at 768 / 1023 / 1440, matching the absence of a Divider node in the tablet and desktop
frames. `[CONFIRMED]`

**Bonus lesson.** The change also removed a stale comment asserting the opposite
("border-top spans full width on mobile…") — *that comment was a rationalisation of the bug,
not a design fact.* Treat a comment that explains why a deviation is fine as a suspect.

### Trap 13 — Fixture/content ordering is a fidelity defect too

Legal links shipped with Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions swapped relative to Figma.
Confirmed from the node widths (66 / 105 / 75 / 86 / 86) — a one-line fixture fix.
`[CONFIRMED]` Node widths are a cheap way to verify content order without reading labels.

---

## (d) JUDGEMENT CALLS — when to ship what the design says, and when to question it

### Ship it, and escalate in parallel

**A Figma nudge artifact.** The CONTACT column's heading sat at `x=4` while its own items and
both other columns' headings sat at `x=0`. ABOUT's heading has no wrapper; CONTACT's sits in
a `wrapper` frame with its text nudged 4px. There is no design reason for one column's
heading to be 4px right of everything around it — it looks like an accidental nudge.

**The call taken:** ship the 4px (it is what the spec says), and ask the designer. Do not
silently align it. `[CONFIRMED]` — and it was later corroborated as intentional when the full
spec tree was pulled: *"Contact heading sits at x=4 — confirms the 4px indent as spec, not a
wart."* The user separately overrode a Figma-faithful removal here, asking for the indent on
three specific items for alignment — a lead's aesthetic call beats a literal read.

**Rule of thumb:** when the design contains something that looks like a mistake, the cheapest
correct action is to reproduce it and raise it. You lose nothing; guessing loses fidelity or
loses the designer's intent.

### Question it — a design gap, not a build defect

**`×` vs `›` on the email field.** Figma's `footer/textfield` showed a close/clear `×` in all
three breakpoint frames (so not a one-frame artefact), while the build rendered a submit
`chevron-right`. Two irreconcilable readings: either the design intends a *clear* affordance
with submit-via-Enter (making our button an invention), or the submit affordance is simply
missing from the design. An `×` conventionally means clear, not submit — and the requirement
(HPC-035) needs a submit that opens a modal, which an `×` cannot be.

**The call taken:** flag it, do not pick one. It changes the interaction model, not just a
glyph. Resolution came from the designer: it is a `›`. `[CONFIRMED]`

**The knock-on, and a good lesson in second-order damage.** A clear-`×` had been built on the
mistaken belief that Figma's glyph was an `×`, with a comment attributing it to the design.
Once the `›` was confirmed, that comment was demonstrably false — and the feature had real
footprint (a conditional button, a recipe part, a hook handler, a unit test, a story `play`).
Two comments in the file turned out to be **exactly inverted**: `trailing-icon` IS in the
extracted spec; the clear-`×` is not.

The resolution was neither "delete it" nor "keep it silently" but **make it an opt-in prop
defaulting off** — which preserves the tested code, makes the empty state match Figma
exactly, and leaves the design question open. `[CONFIRMED]`

**Two sub-rules worth keeping:**
- **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision.** The spec header read
  `managed-by: /extract` / `Status: draft`. "No `clearable` attribute" means the Figma
  *component* exposes no such variant; Figma components routinely do not model transient
  interaction affordances. Absence there is not prohibition.
- **A designer answering a narrower question has not answered the broader one.** "Which
  glyph is that?" ≠ "should the field have a clear affordance?"

### Question it — the design assumes metrics the browser will not give

The subscribe column's 15px of headroom does not survive the +20px cap-height inflation of
two text blocks. That is not a code defect and not fixable in code; it is a design
assumption that needs revisiting with the designer. Similarly, the design's `9px` errorText
is a cap box — `caption` and `body2` both have an 18px line-height, so **no registered text
style produces a smaller line box**. Rendered in a browser, the design's own error block
would be ~26px, not 17. 61px does not exist outside Figma.

### Question it — the design expresses a per-item constraint you can only reproduce systemically

Figma constrained one text node ("ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY") to 118px — the width of its
longest word — forcing a break. That is a per-item decision; the other four items and both
other columns hug naturally. There is no clean CSS rule that reproduces a single-label
constraint, so the build capped the whole column (160px) instead.

Consequences to declare, not hide: About renders 160 (later 115 with `min-content`) against
Figma's 118; the site map is ~70px wider than spec at tablet, which squeezes the
subscribe↔sitemap gap from 100px to 30px. **Adding gap to compensate would be fixing the
wrong thing**, and the arithmetic would break again when the font changed.

The escalation was made concrete by the measurement: *"Figma constrains 'ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF
COUNTRY' per-item to 118px. We cap the column instead, which makes About 42px wider and
closes the gap from 100 to 30 at tablet. Confirm the cap, or specify a per-item rule."*

### Question it — an undesigned state

768–1022px has no frame (Trap 8). The band is real hardware (three iPad models in portrait).
The correct action is declare + escalate + ask for a frame, not invent a third layout.

### The escalation list pattern

Design questions were batched to a named owner with the measurement attached, and split by
type — value-confirmed-token-missing (actionable), value-contested (needs a decision),
value-invented (a guess wearing a token's clothes). The footer's list ran to: the clear-`×`
affordance, column cap vs per-item wrap, the CONTACT 4px indent, the 4.5px nav padding, the
column-heading gap, the 59px `Textfield` slot, the divider colour (50% vs `#ffffff`), icon
stroke weight at 12/16px, 12 SFCC-substituted icons, and 4 icons whose `viewBox` disagrees
with its documented frame.

One genuine token drift surfaced from the comparison and is worth noting as a class: Figma
uses **two distinct greys** in the footer (`text/inverse grey` `#939393` for the subscribe
heading and column headings, `text/inverse/subtle` `#969696` for the legal group) where the
theme collapses both to `#969696`. Three points per channel — imperceptible, but a real
missing token, and inventing it is not an option since the foundation is Tier 1.

---

## (e) WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY

1. **`subscribeBody` text style — `caption` vs `body2`.** The session concluded Figma node
   `1892:50533` binds `Default/body2` (14px / 400) and applied the change, calling it the
   root cause of the user's spacing complaint. The shipped code has `textStyle: 'caption'`
   (12px / 500) with a comment asserting caption. The footer history was squashed, so I
   cannot tell whether this was retracted deliberately. **Recommend re-checking the node.**
   It affects wrapping directly. Both styles share an 18px line-height, so the rendered
   two-line height (36px) cannot discriminate between them.

2. **The final decision on the subscribe error/success structure.** The design-correct
   restructure (padded 68px success box, error appended below, body gap 40→24) was measured,
   verified, and left uncommitted pending the lead's call. `subscribeBody` still carries
   `marginBottom: '3xl'` (40px) and `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` is still 45px. I found no record of
   the decision being taken.

3. **The mobile divider colour.** Shipped as `rgba(255,255,255,0.5)` with the reasoning
   recorded in-code. Figma binds `alias/color/field/border/inverse/default` (`#ffffff`), but
   `get_variable_defs` cannot see layer opacity, so this needed a human visual check. I found
   no record of that check being completed.

4. **Whether the 4.5px nav padding, the column-heading gap (Δ6), and the 59px slot were ever
   answered by the designer.** All three shipped as documented provisionals.

5. **`get_design_context` and `get_screenshot` usage patterns.** My brief listed these, but
   the transcript's assistant-text extract contains almost no direct discussion of them —
   only `get_metadata` and `get_variable_defs` are discussed by name (3 blocks total). Figma
   MCP calls are tool_use blocks, which the extraction pipeline did not capture, so I can
   characterise what was *learned* from each tool but not their exact call patterns. What is
   inferable: `get_metadata` for the node tree and geometry (returns only the queried node —
   no upward traversal); `get_variable_defs` for bound token names and values (blind to layer
   opacity); screenshots for glyph identity and content order, and only at full resolution.

6. **Whether the two Figma files genuinely disagree, or were read at different levels.** The
   design-system footer frame put the subscribe field at y=98 in a 142-tall section
   (implying a 40px body→field gap, which the session verified as "exact"); the composed page
   file puts it at y=82 in a 126-tall section (implying 24px). The session treated the
   composed file as authoritative for states. Whether the design-system symbol is simply
   stale, or whether the 40px is correct for the idle state and 24px only for the error and
   success states, is unresolved — and the two readings imply different fixes.

7. **The `auditTokenUsage.mjs` script** referenced by `overrideStyling.md` as the mechanical
   catch for the sizing/spacing trap **still does not exist**. It was proposed twice as the
   cheap prevention for the worst bug of the session.

# Design Fidelity Against Figma — Transferable Method

Extracted from the SFCC-55 global-footer session (18–21 Aug 2026, PR #59). Domain: reading
Figma geometry correctly, type metrics, CSS layout traps, breakpoints, measurement
methodology, and when to question the design.

Scope note: this file deliberately excludes token/theme architecture, component structure,
and test infrastructure — other agents own those. Where a token fact is load-bearing for a
fidelity decision it appears, but the reasoning stops at the fidelity boundary.

**Confidence convention used below:** `[CONFIRMED]` = measured and re-verified in the
session, or visible in the shipped repo today. `[RETRACTED]` = the session asserted it and
later disproved it; the retraction is the lesson. `[UNVERIFIED]` = stated once, never
re-tested, or I could not confirm it from the repo.

---

## (a) THE METHOD — an ordered procedure from Figma node to verified-fidelity code

This is the sequence that actually worked, reconstructed from what produced findings versus
what produced false alarms. Steps 0–3 are cheap and prevent most of the wasted work.

### Step 0 — Establish which Figma FILE you are in, and get a file key

Two distinct Figma files were in play, and conflating them caused the single largest
misdiagnosis of the session:

| File key | Name | Contains |
|---|---|---|
| `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` | `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` | Component library — symbols, variant sets, `footer/textfield`, `footer-item`, icons |
| `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` | `Zimmermann_Designs` | Composed page designs and **interaction states** (initial / error / success) |

- **A node ID without a file key is unusable.** `footer.ts` cited five nodes
  (`40000407-22493`, `40000407-23484`, `40000461:10415`, `40000538:24875`,
  `40000407:11736`) and the PR body cited two more, all with no file attribution. A
  reviewer could not open any of them. `[CONFIRMED]` Always record
  `<fileKey>/<nodeId>` in code comments and PR bodies.
- If the developer pastes a screenshot of Figma, **the file key is often visible in the
  URL bar in that screenshot** — the session extracted `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` that way and
  needed nothing further from the user. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Step 1 — Enumerate the drawn frames, and note that frames ≠ breakpoints

`get_metadata` on the footer page returned:

| Frame | Node | Viewport width | Frame height |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | `1266:46388` | **1440** | 606 |
| Tablet | `2834:28813` | **1023** | 606 |
| Mobile | `1274:37829` | **402** | 1121 |

Figma's *named breakpoint tokens* are different numbers from its *drawn frames*:

| Token | Value | Drawn frame at that width? |
|---|---|---|
| `alias/breakpoint/tablet` | 768 | **none** |
| `alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide` | 860 | **none** |
| `alias/breakpoint/desktop` | 1024 | none (nearest is 1023) |

`[CONFIRMED]` This gap is not cosmetic — it *is* the defect surface. Our CSS switched to the
side-by-side layout at 768, but the narrowest frame showing that layout is 1023, so
768–1022px rendered a layout the design specifies nowhere. That band was genuinely broken
(see Trap 8).

Tablet drawn at **1023, not 1024**, independently corroborated that `BP.desktop = 64em`
(1024px) was a real design decision rather than a guess.

### Step 2 — Subtract the non-component bands before comparing any height

Each footer frame carried a `Disclaimer` band at the top (breadcrumbs / T&C) that is **not
the footer**:

| | Disclaimer | Dark footer starts at | Footer height to compare against |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 0–130 | y=130 | **476** (not 606) |
| Tablet | 0–130 | y=130 | **476** |
| Mobile | 0–188 | y=188 | **933** (not 1121) |

`[CONFIRMED]` Comparing our 498px render against the frame's 606 would have produced a
108px phantom defect. The `Disclaimer` is a separate component instance (1440×130) and was
correctly absent from the build.

### Step 3 — Classify every Figma node you are about to compare: TEXT node or FRAME/INSTANCE?

**This is the single most valuable discriminator in the whole session.** It decides whether
a reported dimension is directly comparable to CSS or not.

- **FRAME / INSTANCE / COMPONENT node** → the reported height is a real box.
  **Directly comparable to a browser element box.** Chase a delta here.
- **TEXT node** → the reported height is a **cap-height box** (Figma applies
  `text-box-trim: trim-both` / `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). A browser line box is
  taller by the half-leading at each edge. **Not comparable.** A delta here is expected.

Worked examples from the session `[CONFIRMED]`:

| Node | Type | Figma | Ours | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `footer-item` "OUR STORY" | frame | 24 | 24 | comparable, matched |
| `Links` column frame | frame | 134 | 134 | comparable, matched exactly |
| `Textfield` (subscribe field) | **instance** | 44 / 59 | 45 / 68 | comparable — **real gap** |
| "KEEP IN TOUCH" heading | **text** | 8 | 18 | artefact, +10 |
| subscribe body copy | **text** | 26 | 36 | artefact, +10 |
| column heading | **text** | 8 | 14–15 | artefact, +6/7 |
| `errorText` | **text** | 9 | 18 | artefact, +9 |

The clean statement, as it ended up in the shipped `zimmNavItem.ts` comment:

> Figma's text boxes are cap-height (8px one line, 22px two) where a browser line box is
> not, so **the rule transfers rather than the numbers**.

### Step 4 — Take the frame numbers, then DERIVE the CSS rather than copying either number

Once you know which numbers are real, reproduce the *frame* height from type metrics rather
than pasting either side's number. The nav-item fix is the model `[CONFIRMED]`:

```
Figma:   item 24 (one line) / 38 (two lines).  Its text boxes: 8 / 22.
Ours:    line box 15 (14px line-height + 1px underline border reserve); two lines 29.
Derive:  15 + 4.5 + 4.5 = 24    29 + 4.5 + 4.5 = 38    ✅ both exact
Column:  24+24+24+24+38 = 134   = Figma's `Links` frame height exactly
```

Shipped as `lineHeight: var(--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs)` + `paddingBlock: 4.5px`, replacing
`minHeight: 24px` + `alignItems: center`. Note the derivation had to account for a 1px
transparent bottom border on the inner span (the hover-underline mechanism) — chrome that
exists in code and not in the design still enters the arithmetic.

`4.5px` has no entry in `spacing.ts`; it shipped as a documented provisional alongside
`button.ts`'s `BTN_PADDING_Y`, flagged for the designer.

### Step 5 — Make sure the real font is loaded before you measure anything

Any measurement taken under a fallback font is a measurement of the fallback font. See
section (c) Trap 1. Self-hosting Futura Round changed label widths by ~12% and **invalidated
a threshold decision that had already shipped** — the 160px column cap, calibrated against
fallback metrics, started wrapping the label in the wrong place once the real font loaded.

Sequence matters: enable the real font, restart the dev server (HMR leaves stale
`@font-face` rules), *then* re-run the whole geometry suite.

### Step 6 — Measure with Playwright, relative to the component root

The working pattern (from `phase4.mjs`):

```js
import { chromium } from '<abs path>/node_modules/playwright-core/index.mjs';
const b = await chromium.launch();
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: {width: 1440, height: 1400}, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });
await p.goto('http://localhost:3000/', { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded', timeout: 60000 });
await p.waitForSelector('footer[role="contentinfo"]');
await p.waitForTimeout(2500);                       // hydration + font swap
// dismiss the Didomi consent banner or it overlays the measurement
try { const d = p.getByRole('button', {name:/decline/i}).first();
      if (await d.count()) { await d.click(); await p.waitForTimeout(600); } } catch {}
const r = await p.evaluate(() => {
  const f = document.querySelector('footer[role=contentinfo]');
  const top = f.getBoundingClientRect().top;
  const M = e => { const x = e.getBoundingClientRect();
                   return {y: Math.round(x.top - top), h: Math.round(x.height)}; };
  /* ...measure children... */
});
```

Then diff against a hardcoded Figma table in the same script, so the comparison is
reproducible and the expected values are reviewable:

```js
// Figma desktop, relative to the dark footer top (frame 1892:50509, h=476)
const FIG = { footer:{y:0,h:476}, contentRow:{y:0,h:270}, subscribe:{y:64,h:142},
              links:{y:64,h:158}, logoArea:{y:270,h:135}, logo:{y:318,h:39},
              bottomBar:{y:405,h:71}, locale:{y:429,h:23},
              contentRowPad:'64px / 48px', logoAreaPad:'48px / 48px',
              bottomInnerPad:'24px / 24px' };
```

Key points, all `[CONFIRMED]`:

- **Measure `y` relative to the component root**, not the viewport — Figma reports child
  coordinates relative to the parent frame, so this is the only apples-to-apples form.
  `rel = e => ({x: e.getBoundingClientRect().x - base.x, ...})`.
- **`waitUntil: 'networkidle'` never settles on a dev server.** Use `'domcontentloaded'`
  plus an explicit `waitForSelector` and a timeout. This was changed mid-session after
  `networkidle` hung.
- **Dismiss the consent banner first.** The Didomi dev banner painted over the logo and was
  briefly mistaken for a footer defect.
- Also assert **computed paddings as strings** (`'64px / 48px'`) alongside geometry — they
  catch a token that silently failed to resolve, which a height diff can absorb.

### Step 7 — To compare a TEXT dimension, measure the Range, not the element

```js
const rg = document.createRange();
rg.selectNodeContents(el);
rg.getBoundingClientRect();     // the text ink box — comparable to Figma's text node
[...rg.getClientRects()]        // ONE RECT PER LINE BOX
  .filter(r => r.width > 1);    // → line count and per-line widths
```

`[CONFIRMED]` This is how the wrap point was *proved* rather than inferred:

```
1440px  lines = [115, 69]   ← ACKNOWLEDGEMENT / OF COUNTRY  ✅
1280px  lines = [115, 69]  ✅   1023px [115, 69]  ✅
 768px  lines = [115, 69]  ✅    375px [115, 69]  ✅
```

115 and 69 match the measured widths of the two intended lines exactly. An element-height
check (`height > 26 ⇒ wrapped`) tells you *that* it wrapped; only `getClientRects()` tells
you *where*. Also use Range for left-edge alignment checks — the text edge and the box edge
differ, and Figma's `x=4` indent was on the heading *text*, not its box.

### Step 8 — Isolate cause by cumulative in-DOM mutation, before editing source

Rather than editing the recipe and re-rendering per hypothesis, apply candidate fixes as
inline styles in the live page, in sequence, measuring after each. This attributes each
delta to a specific cause `[CONFIRMED]`:

```
stage      item1        item3        icon
current    x=4, y=33    x=4, y=85    y=129
+C         4, 31        4, 79        123     ← li display:flex  (descender leak)
+C+B       0, 31        0, 79        123     ← drop 4px item inset
+C+B+A     0, 31        0, 79        107     ← heading owns the 16px gap
FIGMA      0, 24        0, 72        100
```

Three separate causes, each quantified, plus a **uniform +7 residual everywhere** — and a
uniform residual is the signature of a measurement artefact, not a defect (see Rule R4).

### Step 9 — Sweep the whole responsive range, not just the drawn frames

The widths worth setting `[CONFIRMED]`:

```
 402   mobile frame          ✅
 767   last mobile width     ✅
 768   ← BREAKS              ❌ 18px h-scroll, 7 labels wrap, cols 126/91/71
 860   tablet-wide token     ❌ still broken
 900   mid-band              ❌ cols 149/107/84
1022                         ✅ recovers
1023   tablet frame          ✅ (but subscribe↔sitemap gap 30px vs spec 100px)
1440   desktop frame         ✅
```

**Use the browser device-toolbar and type the width explicitly.** On a retina Mac a
2000px-wide window is ~1000 CSS px — that mis-measurement sent the session down a wrong
path early on. `[CONFIRMED]`

Mobile is not optional: a fix verified only at 1440 can be **masked by a taller sibling
column**. Two separate false negatives came from this (Trap 6).

### Step 10 — Choose the right surface for the check

| Surface | Shows truthfully | Does NOT show |
|---|---|---|
| Local dev server (`localhost:3000`) | Full page, real stacking context, header + footer | — |
| Storybook | Component in isolation, hover/focus states, variant matrix | **No header** → z-index/stacking bugs cannot manifest; base-SFCC SVGs are `ignore-loader`ed so those icons render blank |
| MRT deploy preview | Prefixed storefronts (`/en-ca/`), real bundle paths | Stale unless pushed — see below |
| Vitest / tsc / eslint / CodeRabbit | — | **Nothing about layout.** See Rule R1 |

`[CONFIRMED]` A z-index defect (sticky header 1100 painting over a modal overlay at 1000)
was invisible in Storybook by construction, because `title: 'Layout/Footer'` renders the
footer with no header in the tree.

`[CONFIRMED]` A stale preview is worse than no preview: reviewers logged against a defect
already fixed locally, spending SOW defect budget on code that no longer existed.

### Step 11 — Report each delta with a verdict, not just a number

The output format that worked: for every delta, state **real / artefact / font-driven /
undesigned**, and for anything that isn't "real", say explicitly that fixing it would be
wrong. Example phrasing that stopped a bad fix:

> The heading and body `+10`s are **not** errors — Figma's text boxes are cap-height,
> browser line boxes aren't. Copying 8 and 26 would produce nonsense. I'm flagging that
> explicitly because it's the trap that would make someone "fix" the wrong three numbers.

---

## (b) RULES

**R1 — No automated gate in this stack detects a layout defect.** The single worst bug of
the session (`width: 'xl'` resolving through `theme.sizes` → 576px contact icons → the
global footer destroyed on every page) passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, local CodeRabbit,
remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value,
so TypeScript cannot object; it is a token, so no lint rule fires; nothing asserts layout.
It took the render-beside-Figma pass to find it. `[CONFIRMED]` Budget the visual pass as the
primary defence, not a formality.

**R2 — Classify the node type before comparing any number** (Step 3). Text node → cap-height
box, not comparable. Frame/instance → real box, comparable.

**R3 — Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** Reproduce the design's *mechanism* (equal
leading; height follows the text; the field's edge is anchored and the gap absorbs growth)
and derive the CSS value. Never paste a Figma text-box number into a CSS height.

**R4 — A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a varying one is a defect.** Three
contact items all landing +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's cap-height
box. Items at +7/+9/+14 = three unfound causes. `[CONFIRMED]`

**R5 — Compare like-for-like from ONE file.** The error-state fix was built twice from the
wrong premise because the *initial* state was read from the design-system symbol
(`1892:50509`, field at y=98 in a 142-tall section) while the *error* state came from the
composed page file (`4019:45927`, field at y=82). Within one file the field's top is at y=82
in every state and grows downward. `[CONFIRMED — this is a retraction]`

**R6 — Measurement beats derivation, and three independent measurements beat one
derivation.** A reviewer derived that a submit button computed to 32×32; three measurements
said 16×16. The derivation had missed that Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as
a style prop, which beats the theme size. `[CONFIRMED]`

**R7 — A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source.** `header.ts`'s
`min(597px, 60vw)` / `min(70px, 7.04vw)` appear in exactly three places: the definition, its
own comment explaining the *arithmetic* (`597 = 70 × 631/74`), and a duplicate at the call
site. Nothing says where **70** came from — no Figma node, no `.docs/`, no ticket. By
contrast `zimmLogo`'s 327×39 cites nodes `1892:50472` / `1892:50474` and measured exact.
"Fixing" the header to 597px would have traded quietly wrong for confidently wrong.
`[CONFIRMED]`

**R8 — Ask for the node.** Four times in the session, requesting the node URL took one
message and replaced a derivation with a fact. Distinguish deriving *from the source*
(reproducing the designer's own construction) from deriving *from resemblance* (guessing).

**R9 — An audit matching on value alone produces confident nonsense.** Three "style mirror"
findings were all false positives, and two of the proposed fixes were WCAG 1.4.4
regressions — replacing `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` with `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` looks
equivalent but the token is authored in **px**, which does not scale under zoom. The third
(`SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`) was a coincidental value collision with no
semantic relationship. `[CONFIRMED — this is a retraction]` Check unit and semantic role,
not just the number.

**R10 — Record every accepted deviation, in code and in the PR.** An undeclared deviation
reads to the next developer as an accidental drop and gets "fixed". The footer shipped ~11
declarations in its PR body for exactly this reason.

**R11 — Content-driven widths never reach pixel parity while the font is substituted**, and
the substitution is **per-OS**, so QA on Windows measures different numbers than a developer
on macOS and CI different again. State this as a known class rather than triaging each
instance.

**R12 — Screenshots lie at low resolution.** A locale label read as `[USD]` at low
resolution and was nearly filed as a discrepancy; at full resolution it was
`UNITED STATES (USD) / ENG ›` — identical to ours. Zoom before filing.

**R13 — `get_variable_defs` shows bound variables, not layer opacity.** A stroke bound to
`#ffffff` with the layer at 50% opacity is indistinguishable through the API from an opaque
`#ffffff`. Any colour that might be a 50%-opacity case is "verify visually", not a confirmed
defect. `[CONFIRMED]` — this is why the divider colour shipped unresolved.

**R14 — `get_metadata` returns only the queried node.** You cannot walk up the tree to find
a parent or sibling from a leaf node. Get the frame or component-set URL from the developer.

**R15 — A Figma node's exported path may be rotated relative to its in-frame footprint.**
The chevron exported 15×6 but sat in-frame at 6×15 — the design system draws one glyph and
rotates it. Reproducing that rotation is reproducing the designer's own construction, not
substituting a different icon. Separately, a `viewBox` may disagree with a comment citing
`Size=20`, because "Size=20" is the Figma **variant name**, not the frame. `[CONFIRMED]`

## (c) TRAPS — symptom, root cause, fix

### Trap 1 — Type metrics silently invalidate a threshold decision

**Symptom.** A column cap chosen and verified as correct started wrapping a label in the
wrong place after the real font was self-hosted. `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY` began wrapping
after "OF" instead of after "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT".

**Root cause.** The 160px cap was calibrated against fallback-font metrics. Under Futura
Round every label got ~12% narrower, and `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` dropped to 132.9px — now
inside 160.

**Diagnostic.** Post-font measurements versus Figma:

| Label | Fallback | Futura Round | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| ORDERS & SHIPPING | 120 | **106** | 106 ✅ exact |
| OUR STORY | 68 | **60** | 60 ✅ exact |
| BOOK AN APPOINTMENT | 149 | **131** | 135 |

**Fix.** Re-derive every content-driven threshold after the real font loads. Two prior
findings resolved themselves automatically (the mobile BOOK wrap and an 18px overflow at
768px). `[CONFIRMED]`

**Related trap — `document.fonts.check()` is useless for availability.** It returned `true`
for every family queried, including ones definitively not installed. Only **width comparison
against a known-generic family** is reliable:

```js
const measure = fam => { const s = document.createElement('span');
  s.style.cssText = `position:absolute;white-space:nowrap;font-size:12px;font-weight:500;
    letter-spacing:0;text-transform:uppercase;font-family:${fam}`;
  s.textContent = 'BOOK AN APPOINTMENT'; document.body.appendChild(s);
  const w = s.getBoundingClientRect().width; s.remove(); return Math.round(w*10)/10; };
```

Results: full declared stack **149.1**; `'Futura'` **149.1** (identical → this is what
renders); `'Futura Round'` / `'Futura LT Pro'` / `'Century Gothic'` / `sans-serif` /
`monospace` all **140.7** (→ none installed, all falling through to the same default);
`'Gill Sans'` 137.8; `'Arial'` 143.4.

`[RETRACTED]` The session repeatedly claimed the fallback rendered "Century Gothic / Gill
Sans"; the probe proved it was macOS system **Futura**. And the "~13% wider" figure is
macOS-specific — vs generic sans it is ~6%.

### Trap 2 — A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line

**Symptom.** The ABOUT column sat at its 160px cap with 45px of dead space, pushing the
CONTACT column right and making the site map visibly disproportionate against Figma.

**Diagnostic.**

| Column | Box | Longest line | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABOUT** | **160** | **115** | **45** |
| CONTACT | 135 | 131 | 4 |
| HELP | 105.6 | 105.6 | 0 |

**Root cause.** A wrapped element fills the width available to it. Only the *unwrapped*
siblings hug their content.

**Fix.** `width: min-content` on the wrapped item — resolves to the widest unbreakable run.
Result: About 160→115, slack 45→0, gaps redistributed 99.7→122.2px.

**Must be gated.** Applying it blindly is wrong: `Book an Appointment` went 131→76 and
wrapped. The session gated it on the presence of the NBSP (Trap 3), tying the sizing to the
same signal that already marks the break as intentional:

```tsx
sx={link.fields.label.includes(NBSP) ? { width: 'min-content' } : undefined}
```

`[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:497`.

### Trap 3 — No single threshold can satisfy two constraints; constrain the text instead

**Symptom.** No column cap value could both wrap label A after its first word and keep
label B on one line.

**Diagnostic.**

| Requirement | Constraint |
|---|---|
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT` fits line 1 | cap ≥ 115px |
| `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF` must NOT fit | cap < 132.9px |
| `Book an Appointment` stays one line | cap ≥ 131px |

**Viable window: [131, 132.9) — 1.9 pixels.** That is a coincidence, not a tolerance. Any
hinting difference or one-character copy edit breaks it.

**Fix.** Put the constraint on the phrase, not the container — a non-breaking space:

```ts
label: 'Acknowledgement of Country'
```

With one break opportunity left, the full string cannot fit any cap, so it *must* break
there. Safe window widens from 1.9px to 71px (any cap 115–186px). Use the ` ` escape,
not a literal character — an invisible byte in source is a trap for the next reader.

**Carries a content dependency.** In production this label comes from Contentful, so an
editor must author the NBSP there too; a plain space reverts the wrap. Document it and tell
the content team. `[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `contentfulFixture.ts:56` with that note.

### Trap 4 — `minHeight` + centred alignment loses all leading when content wraps

**Symptom.** The two-line nav label sat flush against the item above it; single-line
siblings looked correctly spaced.

**Diagnostic.**

| Item | box | leading above text |
|---|---|---|
| Our Story / Sustainability / Careers / Brand Protection | 24 | **4.5** |
| **Acknowledgement of Country** | 29 | **0** |

**Root cause.** `minHeight: 24px` + `alignItems: center`. Centring only distributes the
space a *single* line leaves over. Two lines are 29px, which overflows the 24px floor, so
there is nothing to distribute and the leading collapses to zero.

**Fix.** Derive height from `lineHeight` + `paddingBlock` so it holds at any line count.
Keep `minHeight` as the accessibility floor (24px target, WCAG 2.5.8) but stop using it to
*define* the height. Result: exactly 24 / 38, column total 134 = Figma's `Links` frame.

**Nuance worth preserving:** `minHeight` is still the right tool for **reserving** a slot
(so a content swap cannot clip), because it lets the box grow. The trap is only using
`minHeight` + centring to *derive* a height. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Trap 5 — A shorthand resets a longhand declared above it, in your own object

**Symptom.** The first version of the nav-item fix had literally no effect.

**Root cause.** `padding: 0` sat twelve lines *after* `paddingBlock: '4.5px'` in the same
recipe object, and reset it.

**Fix.** `paddingInline: 0` instead of the `padding` shorthand, with a comment so nobody
reintroduces it. `[CONFIRMED]` — shipped at `zimmNavItem.ts:38`.

**Note:** the project's `recipeGuards.test.ts` does *not* catch this — it checks for bare
scale keys inside compound shorthands, not a shorthand resetting a longhand above it. A
known gap.

### Trap 6 — Inline-block / inline-flex descender leak inside a block `<li>`

**Symptom.** Item spacing 26px where Figma had 24, compounding to −6px by the third item.

**Diagnostic.**
```
liDisplay: "list-item"   liHeight: 26
aDisplay:  "inline-flex" aHeight:  24
```

**Root cause.** An `inline-flex` anchor inside a block `<li>` sits on a text baseline, so
the line-box strut adds descender space — measured at ~1.5–2px per row, 9px across five
rows.

**Fix.** `display: flex` on the `<li>`. `[CONFIRMED]` — this was the "C" mutation in Step 8
and closed Δ9 → Δ5 on the links column.

### Trap 7 — Gap ownership: whose 16px is it?

**Symptom.** The contact icon row sat 16px lower than Figma, and only the icon row.

**Root cause.** Figma nests `Icon-list` **inside** the `Links` stack as its 4th child with 0
gap. Our markup made `contactRow` a **sibling of the `<ul>`** inside a `display: flex;
gap: 16px` column — so it collected a gap Figma does not have.

**Fix.** Move the gap from the column to the heading — `linkCol { gap: 0 }` +
`columnHeading { marginBottom: 'm' }` — and move the icon row inside the `<ul>` as its last
`<li>`. `[CONFIRMED]` Whenever a spacing delta affects **one child and not its siblings**,
suspect gap ownership / DOM nesting rather than a wrong value.

### Trap 8 — An undesigned responsive band, and `nowrap` does not prevent shrinking

**Symptom.** Across 768–1022px all five legal links wrapped to two lines each, plus an 18px
horizontal scrollbar at exactly 768px.

**Root cause, in three steps.**
1. At `BP.tablet` (768px) the bottom bar switched from stacked to a single row.
2. That row needs ~845px of content: copyright 185 + five links 468 + six 32px gaps 192. At
   768px only ~554px is available after padding and the locale control.
3. **`flexWrap: nowrap` says "don't break onto a second line" — it does not say "don't
   shrink".** Flex items shrink by default. "TERMS & CONDITIONS" wants 118px and got 70px.
   The row refuses to break, so the words break instead.

**Diagnostic** (simulating the prior `whiteSpace: nowrap`):

| | link widths | link height | page overflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old (`nowrap`) | 74/118/84/96/96 — natural | 31px | **201px** |
| Now (`normal`) | 74/70/43/48/50 — squeezed | 45px | **18px** |

Neither is correct; the underlying defect is identical. Reporting this honestly mattered —
the earlier change had *reduced* the symptom by 90% while leaving the cause.

**Fix considered and DISCARDED.** Moving the row switch to `BP.desktop` (1024) fixed the
band (`ovf 18→0`, `navWrap 7→1`, `legalH 45→31`, 1022px+ byte-identical). It was discarded
because Figma specifies only 402 / 1023 / 1440 and all three already matched — so the change
was not spec compliance but a judgement call about an inferred state, costing +179–236px of
footer height.

**What shipped instead** — declare it and escalate, because the band is iPad portrait:

| Device | Portrait width | |
|---|---|---|
| iPad mini | 744 | below the band |
| iPad 10.2" / Air 11" / Pro 11" | 810 / 820 / 834 | **in it** |
| iPad Pro 13" | 1024 | above it |

Against a ≤10-defect / no-Sev3 contract, "Figma doesn't specify it" is not an accepted
defence once QA logs it. `[CONFIRMED]` One narrower change *was* shipped:
`bottomInner`'s gutter step moved from `BP.desktop` to `BP.tablet`, so the bottom bar stopped
sitting 8px left of the content above it across 768–1023px.

### Trap 9 — Inline vs inline-flex vertical padding, and a 1px chrome border

**Symptom.** "The copyright looks different from the legal links" — while every typographic
property matched byte-for-byte (10px / 500 / 14px line-height / 0.025rem tracking /
uppercase / same colour).

**Root cause.** Box model, not type:

| | Copyright | Legal link |
|---|---|---|
| Element | `<span>` — **inline** | `<a>` — **`inline-flex`** |
| `paddingY: xs` (8px) | applies visually but **does not affect layout height** | contributes to the box |
| Underline-mechanism border | — | **+1px** transparent bottom border on the inner span |
| Total | 30px | **31px** |

`alignItems: center` on the row then centres two *boxes* of different heights, and sub-pixel
rounding surfaces the 0.5px offset as a visible half-line shift. Figma agrees they should
match — it wraps Copyright in a Container frame of height 23, same as the `footer-item`
instances.

**Fix.** Give `copyright` the same box: `display: inline-flex` + `alignItems: center`. A
second finding fell out — `legalLink` carried `height: 'auto'`, silently overriding the
atom's designed 24px, an uncommented deliberate-looking override. `[CONFIRMED]`

### Trap 10 — A perceived SPACING defect can be a TYPE defect

**Symptom.** The user reported the subscribe block's spacing looked wrong.

**Investigation.** Both gaps were verified correct against Figma's own emitted values
(`alias/space/600` = 24px heading→body, `alias/space/1000` = 40px body→field) and matched the
code exactly.

**Root cause found instead.** The body copy was rendering at the wrong text style, so at the
same 200px max-width it wrapped differently — which changed the block height and the rhythm
all the way down to the email field, even though every gap was right.

`[UNVERIFIED / possibly retracted]` The session concluded Figma node `1892:50533` binds
`Default/body2` (14px / 400 / 18px) and changed `caption` → `body2`. **The shipped code today
has `textStyle: 'caption'`** with a comment asserting caption (12px / 500 / 18px). The
footer history was squashed into one commit so I cannot tell whether this was a deliberate
retraction or lost in the squash. **Worth re-checking against Figma** — it materially affects
wrapping, which was the original complaint.

The transferable lesson stands regardless: **before adjusting a gap, verify the type style**,
because wrapping is a function of type metrics and a wrap change reads as a spacing change.

### Trap 11 — Reserving a slot versus reproducing the design's anchoring

This one reversed twice and is the clearest example of getting a fidelity call wrong by
comparing against the wrong node.

**Symptom.** Submitting the subscribe form grew the footer by 22px (slot 45→68, column
163→186, footer 490→512).

**First diagnosis.** The child swaps `<form>` (45px = 36px content + 4/4 padding + 1px
border) for `<p>` (68px = 36px text + 16/16 padding). `subscribeSuccess` carried 32px of its
own vertical padding the form does not have; nothing reserved the slot.

**First fix.** A `subscribeControl` part with `minHeight: 45px`, and strip the message's
padding. Verified Δ0 at 1440 / 768 / 375 / 320.

**The mutation test that mattered.** Removing the padding *alone* showed Δ0 at desktop and
tablet — and that was **coincidence**: the message became 36px, *shorter* than the 45px form,
so the column shrank 9px and the taller site-map column absorbed it. Mobile, where columns
stack, exposed it (Δ−9). `minHeight` was load-bearing, just not where you would look.
**`[CONFIRMED]` Always mutation-test a layout fix at mobile, not desktop.**

**RETRACTION 1.** The session had asserted *"the design's slot is 59px in both states."* It
is not. `footer/textfield` has two variants — `Subscribed=False` 320×44 and `Subscribed=True`
308×59 (narrower too) — and the composed frames show the column staying flat by
**repositioning**: field 44→59 (+15) while the gap above shrinks 40→24 (−16). It is a
compensating reposition, not a reserved slot. Consequence: the subscribed message is a
documented component variant, so implementing it is a build task, not a designer question.

**RETRACTION 2 (the deeper one).** Read like-for-like from the composed page file:

```
                    Textfield        Subscribe Section
initial  4019:45515  y=82  320×44    126
error    4019:45927  y=82  320×61    143   (+17, error appended BELOW the input)
success  4019:46044  y=82  320×59    141   (+15, input replaced by a padded message)
site map                             158   ← 15px spare over the tallest
```

The field's **top stays at y=82 in every state and grows downward**. Neither state jumps —
purely because the column stays shorter than the site map. The success `Textfield` is
`16 + 27 (cap, 2 lines) + 16 = 59`, which in browser terms is `16 + 36 + 16 = 68` — **exactly
what we already had before the "fix"**. The reservation suppressed a growth the design
intends and made the message 23px shorter than specified.

**Why the residual is irreducible:**
```
design  top block  8 + 24 + 26 = 58   → 15px spare over the site map
ours    top block 18 + 24 + 36 = 78   → −6px
                  ───────────────
                  +20px cap-height inflation
```
The design budgeted 15px of headroom that browser text metrics do not leave. That is a real
question for the designer, not a code defect.

**Also found on the way, and a genuine conformance win:** the body's `marginBottom` was 40px
where the composed design specifies **24px** in every state. That 16px inflated the column
and consumed the headroom. Fixing it took @1440 Δ21→Δ5 and @768 Δ7→Δ0.

**Shipped state `[CONFIRMED from the repo]`:** the 45px reserved slot
(`SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT = '2.8125rem'`, commit `9ec0740`), documented as PROVISIONAL with the
59px Figma reference in the comment. The 40→24 gap correction and the design-correct
restructure were **left uncommitted as an open decision** — `subscribeBody` still carries
`marginBottom: '3xl'` (40px) today. The trade was stated as: stillness (Δ0 everywhere, a
deviation) versus structure (matches Figma, Δ5–6 desktop and Δ22–23 mobile). Deferred to the
lead, correctly, after two wrong attempts.

**And a mobile-inherent limit:** the design's anti-jump property *is* headroom beside the
site map. Stacked, there is no neighbour — the design's own section grows 126→143 and would
move everything below it. A jump on mobile is inherent to an in-flow error message; only
reserving or taking it out of flow gives Δ0, and both are deviations.

### Trap 12 — A border cannot be inset

**Symptom.** The mobile divider above the logo ran full-bleed; Figma insets it 20px each
side (`x=20, width=362` in a 402 frame, bound to `alias/space/500`).

**Root cause.** Implemented as `borderTop` on the logo div. A border always spans its
element's full width. Figma models the divider as its own `Container` frame holding a vector.

**Fix.** A pseudo-element with matching `left`/`right` insets:
```ts
position: 'relative',
_before: { content: '""', position: 'absolute', top: 0,
           left: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
           height: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)', background: COLOUR_HALF_INV },
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { _before: { display: 'none' } },
```
Verified: 402px line 20→382; 767px line 20→747 (inset holds at any mobile width); no divider
at 768 / 1023 / 1440, matching the absence of a Divider node in the tablet and desktop
frames. `[CONFIRMED]`

**Bonus lesson.** The change also removed a stale comment asserting the opposite
("border-top spans full width on mobile…") — *that comment was a rationalisation of the bug,
not a design fact.* Treat a comment that explains why a deviation is fine as a suspect.

### Trap 13 — Fixture/content ordering is a fidelity defect too

Legal links shipped with Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions swapped relative to Figma.
Confirmed from the node widths (66 / 105 / 75 / 86 / 86) — a one-line fixture fix.
`[CONFIRMED]` Node widths are a cheap way to verify content order without reading labels.

## (d) JUDGEMENT CALLS — when to ship what the design says, and when to question it

### Ship it, and escalate in parallel

**A Figma nudge artifact.** The CONTACT column's heading sat at `x=4` while its own items and
both other columns' headings sat at `x=0`. ABOUT's heading has no wrapper; CONTACT's sits in
a `wrapper` frame with its text nudged 4px. There is no design reason for one column's
heading to be 4px right of everything around it — it looks like an accidental nudge.

**The call taken:** ship the 4px (it is what the spec says), and ask the designer. Do not
silently align it. `[CONFIRMED]` — and it was later corroborated as intentional when the full
spec tree was pulled: *"Contact heading sits at x=4 — confirms the 4px indent as spec, not a
wart."* The user separately overrode a Figma-faithful removal here, asking for the indent on
three specific items for alignment — a lead's aesthetic call beats a literal read.

**Rule of thumb:** when the design contains something that looks like a mistake, the cheapest
correct action is to reproduce it and raise it. You lose nothing; guessing loses fidelity or
loses the designer's intent.

### Question it — a design gap, not a build defect

**`×` vs `›` on the email field.** Figma's `footer/textfield` showed a close/clear `×` in all
three breakpoint frames (so not a one-frame artefact), while the build rendered a submit
`chevron-right`. Two irreconcilable readings: either the design intends a *clear* affordance
with submit-via-Enter (making our button an invention), or the submit affordance is simply
missing from the design. An `×` conventionally means clear, not submit — and the requirement
(HPC-035) needs a submit that opens a modal, which an `×` cannot be.

**The call taken:** flag it, do not pick one. It changes the interaction model, not just a
glyph. Resolution came from the designer: it is a `›`. `[CONFIRMED]`

**The knock-on, and a good lesson in second-order damage.** A clear-`×` had been built on the
mistaken belief that Figma's glyph was an `×`, with a comment attributing it to the design.
Once the `›` was confirmed, that comment was demonstrably false — and the feature had real
footprint (a conditional button, a recipe part, a hook handler, a unit test, a story `play`).
Two comments in the file turned out to be **exactly inverted**: `trailing-icon` IS in the
extracted spec; the clear-`×` is not.

The resolution was neither "delete it" nor "keep it silently" but **make it an opt-in prop
defaulting off** — which preserves the tested code, makes the empty state match Figma
exactly, and leaves the design question open. `[CONFIRMED]`

**Two sub-rules worth keeping:**
- **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision.** The spec header read
  `managed-by: /extract` / `Status: draft`. "No `clearable` attribute" means the Figma
  *component* exposes no such variant; Figma components routinely do not model transient
  interaction affordances. Absence there is not prohibition.
- **A designer answering a narrower question has not answered the broader one.** "Which
  glyph is that?" ≠ "should the field have a clear affordance?"

### Question it — the design assumes metrics the browser will not give

The subscribe column's 15px of headroom does not survive the +20px cap-height inflation of
two text blocks. That is not a code defect and not fixable in code; it is a design
assumption that needs revisiting with the designer. Similarly, the design's `9px` errorText
is a cap box — `caption` and `body2` both have an 18px line-height, so **no registered text
style produces a smaller line box**. Rendered in a browser, the design's own error block
would be ~26px, not 17. 61px does not exist outside Figma.

### Question it — the design expresses a per-item constraint you can only reproduce systemically

Figma constrained one text node ("ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY") to 118px — the width of its
longest word — forcing a break. That is a per-item decision; the other four items and both
other columns hug naturally. There is no clean CSS rule that reproduces a single-label
constraint, so the build capped the whole column (160px) instead.

Consequences to declare, not hide: About renders 160 (later 115 with `min-content`) against
Figma's 118; the site map is ~70px wider than spec at tablet, which squeezes the
subscribe↔sitemap gap from 100px to 30px. **Adding gap to compensate would be fixing the
wrong thing**, and the arithmetic would break again when the font changed.

The escalation was made concrete by the measurement: *"Figma constrains 'ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF
COUNTRY' per-item to 118px. We cap the column instead, which makes About 42px wider and
closes the gap from 100 to 30 at tablet. Confirm the cap, or specify a per-item rule."*

### Question it — an undesigned state

768–1022px has no frame (Trap 8). The band is real hardware (three iPad models in portrait).
The correct action is declare + escalate + ask for a frame, not invent a third layout.

### The escalation list pattern

Design questions were batched to a named owner with the measurement attached, and split by
type — value-confirmed-token-missing (actionable), value-contested (needs a decision),
value-invented (a guess wearing a token's clothes). The footer's list ran to: the clear-`×`
affordance, column cap vs per-item wrap, the CONTACT 4px indent, the 4.5px nav padding, the
column-heading gap, the 59px `Textfield` slot, the divider colour (50% vs `#ffffff`), icon
stroke weight at 12/16px, 12 SFCC-substituted icons, and 4 icons whose `viewBox` disagrees
with its documented frame.

One genuine token drift surfaced from the comparison and is worth noting as a class: Figma
uses **two distinct greys** in the footer (`text/inverse grey` `#939393` for the subscribe
heading and column headings, `text/inverse/subtle` `#969696` for the legal group) where the
theme collapses both to `#969696`. Three points per channel — imperceptible, but a real
missing token, and inventing it is not an option since the foundation is Tier 1.

## Summary

Full findings: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f/scratchpad/agent-figma.md` (11-step method, 15 rules, 13 traps, judgement calls, 7 unverified items).

**The highest-value finding — a node-type discriminator, not a fudge factor.** Figma text nodes report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both` / `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`); frames and instances report a real box. Text nodes are *not* comparable to CSS line boxes; frames are. This decides whether a delta is chaseable: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18 are all artifacts, while the `Textfield` **instance** at 44/59 vs our 45/68 was a genuine gap. The rule that fell out — *"transfer the rule, not the numbers"* — is in the shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, where deriving from `lineHeight + 4.5px padding` landed 24/24/24/24/38 = 134, exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

**Corollary heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's cap box.

**Three retractions that are the real lessons.** (1) *"The design's slot is 59px in both states"* was wrong — `Subscribed=False` 320×44, `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24; the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve. The subsequent "reserve the slot" fix was then also wrong: the 68px padded box we already had was design-correct, and the reservation suppressed intended growth. Root cause of both: comparing the initial state from the design-system symbol (`1892:50509`, field y=98) against the error state from the composed page file (`4019:45927`, field y=82). **Two Figma files exist** — `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (page states) — and comparisons must be like-for-like from one. (2) A "style mirror" fix replacing `'3rem'` with `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — the token is authored in px. (3) The fallback font was macOS system Futura, not Century Gothic; `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — only width comparison works.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through `theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the global footer on every page — passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only the render-beside-Figma pass found it.

**Method essentials:** subtract the non-footer `Disclaimer` band (compare against 476, not 606); measure `y` relative to the component root, since Figma reports frame-relative coordinates; use `domcontentloaded` (`networkidle` never settles on a dev server); dismiss the consent banner first; use `Range.getClientRects()` for per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point; isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked them.

**Frames ≠ breakpoints:** frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed 768–1022 band was genuinely broken (18px h-scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and covers three iPad models in portrait — `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking, so the row refused to break and the words broke instead.
